pages.text: $(item)LPG$() comes from the top output of a crude oil tower: 60 mB per run. In a chemical vat it can be split and put back together:
$(l)Separation$()$(br)$(item)1000 mB LPG$() gives $(item)500 mB butane + 500 mB propane$(). Use any chemical vat with a $(item)Freezer$() attached.

$(l)Compression$()$(br)$(item)500 mB butane + 500 mB propane$() give $(item)1000 mB LPG$(). This needs a $(item)Compressor$() pressurising the vat, and only works in a $(item)steel$() or $(item)fireproof$() chemical vat.$(br2)$(l)Uses$()$(li)All three are firebox fuels and burn in flarestacks and gas lamps.

$(li)A spout fills an $(item)engine cylinder$() with 250 mB of butane or propane, to run an engine on that gas.$(li)A spout turns an empty bucket and 1000 mB of LPG into an $(item)LPG tank$(), handy to carry gas by hand.

LPG is also a strong reason to keep the six-output crude oil tower: the five-output recipe makes as much, but the three-output one makes none. The chemical vat chapter explains how to attach freezers and compressors.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
